deck: Table Rock this morning: 910.61 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Don't quit at 10.
play.body: Fall is the opposite of August. The bite can last until lunch.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

tomorrow: Tomorrow we print a new level, a new play, and whether the dam spun overnight. Open it before you drive. The water will have moved.
weekGraf: The pool walked down from 910.82 early in the week to 910.61 this morning — about 0.21 ft off that earlier mark, still under the 915 full pool. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.temp: Verify at the ramp — scout does not invent dawn temps
now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: At just over 4 ft below full pool, more shoreline, stumps, and hazards are exposed in the coves, creek arms, and near some ramps. Boat slowly, especially up the James, Kings, and Long Creek arms, and double-check launch conditions.

Surface water has cooled into the upper 60s with exceptional clarity. Bass hit topwaters and soft plastics early, then move to jigs, live bait, or drop-shot rigs around long points, gravel flats dropping into 20–40 feet, and offshore structure. Mixed-bag action includes walleye on points in 20–25 ft and crappie/spotted bass from deeper brush and docks. Clean presentations in this clear, cooling water continue to produce solid catches.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~9,220 cfs on the last printed reading. Not a live hourly. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: This cold tailwater fed by deep releases from Table Rock stays productive year-round thanks to consistent stocking. Generation is the primary tactic book: low or minimal flows early create excellent windows for wading, light-line drifting, or indicator fishing with micro jigs, midges, scuds, worms, or Gulp eggs. When current builds (typically afternoon into evening), switch to weighted rigs and target seams and structure.

From Table Rock Dam down to Fall Creek is trophy water — artificial lures and flies only; no soft plastics or scented/natural baits. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Save pink worms, PowerBait, Gulp eggs, or other soft plastics/scented baits for water below Fall Creek. A trout permit is required in many sections. Recent reports highlight improving rainbow numbers, active browns in the upper lake, slow dock fishing but better boat catches on worms and eggs, and productive wading with Pink PowerWorm when flows are off. Water clarity is generally good. Call 866-494-1993 for the latest SWPA schedule before heading out.

editor.note: Two-lake daily rebuilt from the morning fishing scout plus the prior week of files. We print a level only when the scout had one. Carry-forward mornings are labeled. No invented bite ratings. Call 866-494-1993 before wading Taneycomo.
